qa_pairs.instruction: What is the purpose of the Triggerless Future Event Processing policy in the JDBC driver?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver, the Triggerless Future Event Processing policy is an example that checks a user's "commence" attribute, determines whether the associated event time is in the future relative to the database's current time, and, if so, returns a retry status so the event can be processed later. It demonstrates how to retrieve attribute values, parse timestamps, compare them, and conditionally control processing flow without triggering an explicit event.

qa_pairs.instruction: How does the rule "Break if commencement date unavailable" function within the JDBC driver policy?
qa_pairs.output: In the JDBC driver policy, the "Break if commencement date unavailable" rule checks the local variable named "commence" that was set earlier. The condition `<if-local-variable name="commence" op="equal"/>` evaluates to true when the variable is empty or not set. When the condition matches, the `<do-break/>` action stops further rule execution, preventing the policy from attempting to parse or compare timestamps when no commencement date exists.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you construct a policy in the JDBC driver to detect and retry future events based on a "commence" attribute?
qa_pairs.output:
To construct such a policy in the JDBC driver, follow these steps:
1. Define the policy XML and include the required namespaces for Timestamp, TimestampUtil, and jdbc.
2. Add a rule that retrieves the "commence" attribute from the user object and stores it in a local variable named `commence` using `<do-set-local-variable>`.
3. Add a second rule that checks if `commence` is empty; if it is, use `<do-break/>` to stop further processing.
4. Add a rule to parse the database time and the event time:
   - Use `<do-set-local-variable name="dbTime">` with `<token-xpath expression="Timestamp:valueOf(@jdbc:database-local-time)"/>`.
   - Use `<do-set-local-variable name="eventTime">` with `<token-xpath expression="Timestamp:valueOf($commence)"/>`.
5. Add a rule to compare the two timestamps:
   - Use `<do-set-local-variable name="after">` with `<token-xpath expression="TimestampUtil:after($eventTime, $dbTime)"/>`.
6. Add a final rule that checks if the variable `after` equals "true"; if so, return a retry status using `<do-status level="retry">` with a message like "Future event detected.".
7. Close the policy element.
This sequence implements triggerless future event detection and retry handling in the JDBC driver.

qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize the key steps of the example policy for triggerless future event processing in the JDBC driver.
qa_pairs.output: The example policy for triggerless future event processing in the JDBC driver performs the following steps: (1) Retrieves the user’s `commence` attribute into a local variable; (2) Breaks execution if `commence` is missing; (3) Parses the database’s current time and the event’s commencement time into `Timestamp` objects; (4) Uses `TimestampUtil:after` to determine if the event time is later than the database time; (5) If the event is in the future, issues a retry status with the message "Future event detected.".

qa_pairs.instruction: Provide the complete XML policy example for triggerless future event processing as used in the JDBC driver.
qa_pairs.output:
<policy    xmlns:Timestamp="http://www.novell.com/nxsl/java/java.sql.Timestamp"
  xmlns:TimestampUtil="http://www.novell.com/nxsl/java/com.novell.nds.dirxml.driver.jdbc.db.TimestampUtil"
  xmlns:jdbc="urn:dirxml:jdbc">
<rule>
<description>Get commencement date from datasource.</description>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-xpath op="true">.</if-xpath>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-set-local-variable name="commence">
      <arg-string>
        <token-src-attr class-name="User" name="commence"/>
      </arg-string>
    </do-set-local-variable>
  </actions>
</rule>

<rule>
  <description>Break if commencement date unavailable.</description>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-local-variable name="commence" op="equal"/>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-break/>
  </actions>
</rule>

<rule>
<description>Parse times.</description>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-xpath op="true">.</if-xpath>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-set-local-variable name="dbTime">
      <arg-object>
        <token-xpath expression="Timestamp:valueOf(@jdbc:database-local-time)"/>
      </arg-object>
    </do-set-local-variable>
    <do-set-local-variable name="eventTime">
      <arg-object>
        <token-xpath expression="Timestamp:valueOf($commence)"/>
      </arg-object>
    </do-set-local-variable>
  </actions>
</rule>
<rule>
<description>Is commencement date after database time?</description>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-xpath op="true">.</if-xpath>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-set-local-variable name="after">
      <arg-string>
        <token-xpath expression="TimestampUtil:after($eventTime, $dbTime)"/>
      </arg-string>
    </do-set-local-variable>
  </actions>
</rule>

<rule>
<description>Retry if future event.</description>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-local-variable name="after" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-status level="retry">
      <arg-string>
        <token-text xml:space="preserve">Future event detected.</token-text>
      </arg-string>
    </do-status>
  </actions>
</rule>
</policy>
